objection.quote:
Thus $V$ contains **at most one** positive number.  Consequently, either  

* (i) $g\equiv 0$ (constant), which gives $f(x)=x$, a solution; or  
* (ii) there is $c>0$ such that $V \subseteq \{0, c\}$ with both values attainable.
objection.witness: The argument has shown only that two distinct positive values cannot occur; it has not written an argument excluding negative values of $g$. To cover all cases it must prove that $g(t)<0$ is impossible by iterating the orbit until $t+n g(t)\le0$. Without that step, the asserted dichotomy and all subsequent level-set arguments omit a case.
objection.load_bearing: Sections 4–6 assume every point lies in $S_0\cup S_c$. Thus the claimed constancy of $g$ depends on the unwritten exclusion of negative differences.
